newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads - Rebound against the U.S.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads - Rebound against the U.S.

text.p: The Australian bond market generally outperformed against the dollar bloc as the prospect of a bond-friendly federal budget on May 13 started to be priced in, traders said.

The long end narrowed sharply to the U.S., and has reclaimed nearly all the lost ground which occured after last week's stronger than expected average weekly earnings data when the 10-year spread to the U.S. blew out to over 120 basis points.
This strong outperformance was despite another advance in U.S. Treasuries following a balance budget accord in Washington on Friday.
There was no trading in U.S. Treasuries in Asia due to a holiday in Japan.

Only the short end of the Canadian market stayed wider against Australia on the day, having outperformed the U.S. Friday amid a strong Canadian dollar on hopes that the Federal Open Market Committee will keep U.S. policy on hold when it meets on May 20.
